newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka tourism revival to boost hotel stocks.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka tourism revival to boost hotel stocks.

text.p: Sri Lanka's hotel sector stocks are expected to rise in 1997 thanks to a revival in the tourist industry which saw a 25 percent drop in arrivals in 1996, analysts said on Friday.

The recovery is being fuelled by tight security in the capital Colombo and its suburbs, which have been put on high alert after Tamil Tiger rebels attacked an oil depot in 1995 and bombed the Central Bank and a crowded commuter train in 1996, they said. The country's earnings from tourism plunged to $175 million in 1996 from $225 million the previous year, reducing it to a low-budget destination.
A fall in arrivals saw many with exposure to tourism put investments on hold. Hotel companies also began to undercut each other, sometimes selling a $85 resort hotel room for $40, hotel sources said.

Apart from hotel companies, an upturn in tourism will also have a favourable impact on the 1997 performance of the three blue chip conglomerates which are exposed to the sector, says brokerage Jardine Fleming in a March strategy report.
The three blue chips are John Keells Holdings Ltd, Hayleys Ltd and Aitken Spence & Co.
"We believe the tourist sector has clearly bottomed out and the only way is up," the report said.

"We have already seen a turnaround in the first quarter of this year. If the trend lasts, arrivals in 1997 should be close to the 1995 figure of 407,000," said Jagath Fernando, diretor of John Keells Holdings Ltd, Sri Lanka's largest inbound tour operator.

The group has seven companies listed in the hotel and travel sector of the Colombo Stock Exchange - Beruwala Walk Inn, Ceylon Holiday Resorts, Habarna Lodge, Habarana Walk Inn, International Tourist & Hoteliers, Kandy Walk Inn and Walkers Tours.
Through them it owns and manages 1,100 hotel rooms in Sri Lanka and 80 in the Maldives and is agent for five major European tour operators.

"Once upon a time tourism contributed nearly 40 percent to group profits. If 1997 remains calm we will break even on the Sri Lankan side and make a profit of 20 million rupees on the Maldives," Fernando said.

Sri Lanka Tourist Board officials say there are signs of a definite recovery. Board chairman H.M.S. Samaranayake told Reuters recently that there was a 15 percent increase in tourist traffic in January and February this year.
Airline officials too say there has been a substantial rise in tourist traffic to Colombo.

"Current quarter load factor is over 87 percent on each flight compared to about 60 percent in the first quarter of 1996," said Joe Rajadurai, British Airways country manager for Sri Lanka and the Maldives.
British Airways has two flights a week to Colombo.
Listed company shares in Colombo have been quick to respond to the good news and gained about five percent in March, analysts said.

"Although we expect above average growth from the domestic hotel industry due to the rebound from depressed levels, we believe that the industry's earnings will remain volatile," cautioned Jardine Fleming.
The Colombo Stock exchange all share index which closed at 636.86 points on Thursday, has gained five percent or 30 points this year due to good profits in the last quarter 1996.
